deck_en: A measured excess, a verified shipment and a political break. Evidence can constrain a decision without making the decision for us.
deck_zh: 一次超量、一批得到核实的外运，还有后来的政治分歧。证据能够约束判断，却不能代替判断。

body_zh: 2016年11月8日，国际原子能机构核实，伊朗重水库存达到130.1公吨。协议所估计的当时需求水平是130吨，超出部分应供出口。多出来的小数点后一位，被写进了报告。[1][2]
随后，伊朗报告在11月19日运出11吨；12月6日，机构在伊朗境外的目的地核实了这批重水。[1]发现、告知、运出、核实，不是同一时刻完成的动作。把它们分开记，才看得出一项承诺到底怎样落地。
这个数既不能被轻轻抹成“差不多”，也不会自己跳起来，宣布整个协议应该结束。它让偏差有了可回查的形状。但偏差有多重要，纠正是否足够，接下来应当怎么做，还需要另外的理由。
外交新闻常把一个协议写成一种立场：支持它，或者反对它。130.1吨把我们暂时带到更小的地方。先别急着站队。这里确实有一件被发现、被处理、又被别人核对过的事。它能说明什么？又不能替什么担保？
## 数字让哪些话不再只靠保证
2015年，伊朗与中国、法国、德国、俄罗斯、英国、美国及欧盟方面达成全面协议，通常简称JCPOA。它安排了一组核相关限制、透明措施和相应的制裁缓解。达成文本，不等于所有动作当日都已完成。[2]
2016年1月16日成为实施日，是因为国际原子能机构核实，附件V指定的一组准备措施已经落实。[3]这个判断有明确对象。它不是宣布伊朗过去从未有过问题，也不是替未来所有意图出具一份永久保证。
协议的力量之一，正在于缩小某些句子的范围。与其只问“你究竟想做什么”，不如有一些地方能够具体问：约定的库存是多少，哪些设备在运行，哪些记录可以持续核对？担忧没有消失，却有一部分不必永远停在猜测里。
130吨也不是凭空落下的一道自然界限。附件I第十四段把它写成现代化阿拉克反应堆投运前的需求估计，并要求超出需求的重水供出口。[2]具体文件怎样写，关系到后来怎样判断；不能只留下一个数字，再由作者替它补上所有法律后果。
所以，2016年11月的130.1吨值得保留。若为了说明协议有用，就把不便的偏差删掉，等于先拿走核查真正做过的工作。可若把一次超量直接写成所有承诺都已崩塌，也同样跳过了外运和核实的后续。
这不是替偏差寻找好听的名字。记录之所以有用，是因为它不让任何一方只挑自己需要的那一句。发现确实发生了，纠正也有记录。评价要面对这两个事实，而不是任意选择其中一个。
核查机构因此需要专业判断。数据从哪里来，怎样确认，能够支持哪种结论，都不是机器自己讲完的话。但这种专业判断有任务边界：核材料与相关承诺的核查，不会自动延伸为对一个国家所有军事、外交与地区行为的总裁判。
## 连“算多少”也需要说明
另一个细节，让事情不再只是看一张数字表那么简单。2017年的报告讨论了伊斯法罕一处工厂生产线里留存的材料。联合委员会1月10日作出相关决定，月底开始执行相应处理；2月19日，伊朗才正式提交99.9公斤浓缩铀的修订估算，机构认为与自己的评估一致。[1]
99.9这个数看起来不小，可它说的是铀的质量；库存上限中的300公斤，说的却是六氟化铀等值。计量对象不同，不能直接比大小。至于是否计入总量，还须看联合委员会决定所附的条件。读懂数字，有时先要读懂数字后面的单位。[1]
普通读者不必记住这些数字。但它们提醒我们，公布一个上限，还没有做完全部工作。什么算进来、用什么单位、按什么条件处理，都影响“没有超出”这句话究竟在说什么。数字可以很精确，句子的前提仍然需要解释。
这也使公开说明重要。若只让公众看到最后一个合计数，却看不到核算依据怎样变化，支持者会把它读成毫无疑问的履约，反对者则可能把每项解释都读成偷偷放宽。可以回查的依据，未必消除分歧，却至少让分歧有一个具体对象。
协议还有争议解决程序，不能把国际原子能机构的技术报告想成唯一一条路。参与者可以把履约争议交到联合委员会，并按文件规定进入进一步处理；争议仍未解决时，是否构成重大不履行，也并非由一个测量值自动决定。[2]
这里的分别，不是让政治从证据面前逃走。恰恰相反：如果要说偏差严重，就要解释严重在哪里；如果要说纠正已经足够，也要说明为什么。不能因为最后仍须有人判断，就把此前核实过的事实重新变成可有可无。
2018年5月的报告把认识边界说得很清楚：机构继续核实已申报核材料未被转用，但对不存在未申报核材料和活动的评价仍在进行。[4]这两句话并不矛盾。没有确认某种未申报活动，不等于已经完成了对其不存在的证明。
可反过来，“评价仍在进行”也不是已经发现秘密活动的同义词。若把每项未完成判断都当作有罪证据，检查越诚实地写明自己的边界，就越容易被读成什么也不值得相信。这样的读法，最后只会奖励不肯承认边界的保证。
## 报告还在继续，决定已经分开
2018年5月8日，特朗普宣布美国停止参与协议，恢复相关制裁的程序随之启动。他公开给出的理由包括协议期限、未来核风险、导弹和地区安全等问题。[5]这些是美国政府的政策判断和主张，不是国际原子能机构替它作出的技术结论。
英法德领导人同日表达相反判断：根据机构报告，伊朗仍遵守协议规定的限制，因此应维持协议。[6]双方并不只是在争论同一张表有没有算对，也在争论一份范围有限的交换，还值不值得继续。
5月24日，机构发布的新报告仍逐项列出核查情况，记录了相关库存与浓缩水平没有超出所述限制，并保留了对未申报活动的认识边界。[4]报告没有因为政治关系破裂，就自动改写成一个相反的技术答案。
反对维持协议的一方，最有力的问题可以是：这些限制即使当下运行，能否应对较远的风险和没有被纳入协议的问题？支持维持的一方，则可以问：既然某些风险已经受到可核查的限制，取消这份安排会留下什么，替代办法又怎样实现？
没有哪一边可以只用自己的问题，把另一边的问题从纸上划掉。有限协议不等于所有风险已解决；存在协议以外的风险，也不自动证明协议内部的限制没有价值。若要扩大合作目标，还要解释怎样取得新的共同授权，而不是把新要求倒写成旧承诺。
普通人的生活又隔着一段传导。2016年实施日的制裁缓解，针对列明的核相关措施，不是所有制裁一齐消失。[7]一项交易在法律上重新被允许，与银行愿意办理、企业得到融资，还不是同一件事。
国际货币基金组织2017年的同期研究记录了银行联系恢复，也指出大型银行仍然缺席；剩余制裁、执法风险、反洗钱与融资透明度问题等都在起作用。[8]不能用“制裁解除了”替每个家庭写出生活改善，也不能因传导受阻，就说这段缓解没有带来任何改变。
这使继续还是停止，不能只留在谈判者的安全语言里。判断可以不同，但须说明预期收益、替代办法和可能由别人承担的代价。技术核查不包办这些理由；它的边界也不意味着，作决定的人从此不必给出理由。
本文停在2015至2018年这段历史，不拿后来的事件替当时所有参与者补上一双预知未来的眼睛。那时已经可以看见的，是一套核查在运作，一些问题得到具体处理，各方对这套安排是否足够却作出了不同决定。
130.1吨的意义，也许正在这里。证据让人少了一些可以随意说的话，却没有让人免去判断的责任。小数点已经写下。接下来谁决定，依据什么决定，决定以后又由谁承担，仍然要继续问。
body_en: On 8 November 2016, the International Atomic Energy Agency verified that Iran’s heavy-water stock had reached 130.1 metric tonnes. The agreement estimated needs at 130 tonnes at that stage and provided for excess material to be made available for export. The decimal place entered the record.[1][2]

Iran subsequently reported that 11 tonnes had left the country on 19 November. On 6 December, the Agency verified the quantity at its destination abroad.[1] Discovery, notification, shipment and independent confirmation were separate events. Keeping them separate makes it possible to see how a commitment was actually implemented, rather than merely announced.

The excess cannot be rounded away as close enough. Nor can a decimal place pronounce the end of an entire agreement. It gives the discrepancy an identifiable form. How serious it was, whether the response was adequate and what should follow still require reasons. The quantity does not contain its own complete judgment.

Diplomatic coverage often turns an agreement into a position to support or oppose. The figure 130.1 lets us start somewhere smaller. Something was detected, addressed and checked by another organization. Before choosing a verdict on the whole arrangement, we can ask what this sequence establishes—and what it cannot guarantee.
## What a number can take out of the realm of promises

In 2015, Iran and China, France, Germany, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States, with the European Union’s High Representative, agreed the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action. The JCPOA combined specified nuclear measures, transparency arrangements and sanctions relief. Agreeing the text was not the same event as completing every action it envisaged.[2]

Implementation Day followed on 16 January 2016, when the IAEA verified completion of the preparatory nuclear measures specified in Annex V.[3] That finding had an object. It was not a declaration that Iran’s entire past was unproblematic, nor a permanent assurance about every future intention. A particular conclusion should not acquire a larger meaning merely because the agreement matters politically.

One strength of the arrangement was precisely its ability to make some questions smaller. Rather than relying entirely on assurances about intentions, participants could check specified stocks, equipment and records. Anxiety did not disappear. A portion of it could be addressed through repeatable observations instead of remaining indefinitely a dispute about what another government might secretly want.

The 130-tonne figure was not a boundary supplied by nature. Annex I, paragraph 14, set it out as an estimate of needs before the modernized Arak reactor entered service, with excess heavy water to be offered for export.[2] The wording matters. An author cannot retain a number and then invent all the legal consequences that are supposed to accompany it.

That is why the November figure deserves to stay. Removing an inconvenient excess to demonstrate that verification worked would remove something verification actually did. Treating the same excess as immediate proof that all commitments had collapsed would omit the shipment and the subsequent check. Neither account would preserve the sequence it purported to explain.

This is not a search for a flattering name for a discrepancy. A record is useful because it prevents either side from selecting only the sentence it needs. There was a detected excess. There was also a documented response. An evaluation has to encounter both, rather than treating them as rival versions from which it may choose freely.

Verification consequently requires professional judgment: assessing information, checking it and deciding which conclusion it supports. That professional task has limits. Monitoring nuclear materials and specified commitments does not automatically make the Agency the judge of every military, diplomatic or regional activity of a state. Its expertise does not become unlimited merely because the political stakes are high.
## Even a total has premises

Another episode complicates the image of a simple numerical test. A 2017 report addressed material retained in process equipment at Esfahan. A Joint Commission decision was made on 10 January; the associated treatment began later that month. Iran submitted its revised estimate of 99.9 kilograms of enriched uranium on 19 February, which the Agency found consistent with its assessment.[1]

The number may appear substantial. But kilograms of uranium cannot be directly compared with a limit expressed in kilograms of uranium hexafluoride or its equivalent. The accounting treatment was also subject to conditions in the Commission’s decision.[1] Precision about a number includes precision about what is being counted. A decimal place does not make its unit unnecessary.

Readers need not memorize those quantities. Their importance lies in the premises behind a total: which material counts, in which units and under which agreed conditions. A result can be numerically precise while still depending on a definition that needs explaining. Measurement does not eliminate interpretation; sometimes it makes a previously hidden interpretive question visible.

Public explanations matter for that reason. If people see only a final total without its accounting basis, supporters may read certainty into it while opponents read every clarification as a concealed concession. Accessible reasons will not remove disagreement. They can give disagreement something definite to address, rather than requiring it to revolve entirely around suspicion.

The agreement also provided a dispute-resolution route. Participants could refer a performance concern to the Joint Commission and pursue further procedures set out in the text. Whether an unresolved matter constituted significant non-performance was not a verdict automatically generated by a measuring device.[2] A technical report was important without being the only institutional document that mattered.

This distinction should not become an escape route from evidence. Anyone calling a discrepancy serious must explain why it is serious. Anyone calling a correction sufficient must explain that too. The fact that a judgment remains to be made does not make established observations optional. Different responsibilities ought to make the account more demanding, not less.

The Agency’s May 2018 report marked an especially important boundary. It continued to verify non-diversion of declared nuclear material, while its evaluation of the absence of undeclared material and activities remained ongoing.[4] Those statements did not contradict one another. A finding about declared material cannot simply be enlarged into proof that every possible undeclared activity has been ruled out.

The converse is equally necessary. An evaluation still under way is not itself a discovery of secret activity. If every incomplete conclusion is converted into incriminating evidence, honest qualification becomes indistinguishable from failure. The institution that acknowledges its limits is then punished for the very precision that makes its reports useful, while an unlimited assurance becomes easier to sell.
## The reports continued; the decisions diverged

On 8 May 2018, President Trump announced that the United States would cease participating in the agreement and begin restoring relevant sanctions. His public reasons included the agreement’s duration, longer-term nuclear risks, missiles and regional security.[5] These were the administration’s claims and policy assessment. They were not a technical judgment made on its behalf by the IAEA.

The British, French and German leaders reached a different conclusion that day. Referring to IAEA reporting, they considered Iran to be abiding by the agreement’s restrictions and argued for retaining it.[6] The disagreement was not merely about whether the same column had been added correctly. It concerned whether a deliberately limited exchange remained worth maintaining.

On 24 May, a new IAEA report continued to list the results of monitoring, recording stocks and enrichment levels within the specified limits while preserving its qualifications about undeclared activities.[4] A political rupture had not automatically converted the technical account into its opposite. The report still had to say what the Agency could substantiate.

A serious objection to retaining the agreement could ask whether functioning present restrictions were sufficient for longer-term risks and activities outside its scope. A serious argument for retaining it could ask what would remain after removing verified constraints, and how a better alternative could actually be obtained. Neither question is frivolous merely because it is not the other side’s preferred question.

A limited agreement does not establish that every relevant danger has been solved. Dangers beyond its scope do not automatically establish that restrictions inside it have no value. Expanding the purpose of cooperation requires an account of how new commitments can be agreed, rather than silently treating additional demands as if they had always been part of the original bargain.

Ordinary life lies at a further distance. Implementation Day relief concerned specified nuclear-related sanctions; it did not remove every sanction.[7] Legal permission for some transactions is different from a bank’s willingness to process them, or a business’s ability to obtain finance. The path from an international announcement to an available service has more than one decision-maker along it.

The IMF’s contemporaneous 2017 study recorded restored banking relationships, but also the continuing absence of major banks. Remaining sanctions, enforcement risk, anti-money-laundering weaknesses and transparency concerns were among the obstacles.[8] Relief cannot stand as proof of improvement for every household. Equally, obstructed transmission does not establish that no beneficial change occurred. Neither extreme follows from the available account.

The choice to continue or stop therefore cannot be explained only in the security vocabulary of negotiators. Assessments may differ, but they still need to address expected benefits, alternatives and costs borne by others. Verification cannot supply all those reasons. Its inability to supply them is not permission for decision-makers to stop offering reasons themselves.

This essay remains within 2015–2018. Later events cannot provide every participant with knowledge unavailable at the time. What the contemporary record already shows is verification operating, particular issues receiving concrete responses and participants disagreeing about the adequacy of the arrangement. Keeping that combination intact is more revealing than reading the whole period backwards from a later outcome.

Perhaps that is what the decimal place leaves us with. Evidence reduces what can be said arbitrarily without relieving anyone of the responsibility to judge. The figure has been entered. Who decides next, on what grounds, and at whose cost are still questions requiring an answer.
